summary: BigBear.ai is a small-cap ($1.94B market cap; E6) AI decision-intelligence provider that is deeply unprofitable and contracting: operating margin is -66.9% and net margin -226.7% (E11, E12), while revenue fell to ~$0.1B in 2025 from ~$0.2B in 2022-2024 (E24) with -0.9% YoY in the latest quarter (E9). It is burning cash (TTM FCF -$59.49M; E14) but retains a sizeable net-cash cushion ($349.39M cash vs $24.11M debt; E16, E17) and strong liquidity (current ratio 6.08; E19) that funds multi-year runway. Valuation is hard to justify on fundamentals given a negative forward P/E (E7) and a high implied price/sales on ~$0.1-0.2B of revenue, though a thin 3-analyst mean target of $5.33 (E3) sits ~32% above the $4.05 price (E2). Critically, no competitive or moat data is available (E25), and the overall risk profile is high given cash burn, revenue decline, and a 3.08 beta (E20).

dimensions.rationale: Latest-quarter revenue declined -0.9% YoY (E9), and the annual revenue trend fell from ~$0.2B across 2022-2024 to ~$0.1B in 2025 (E24), indicating contraction rather than growth. The negative forward P/E of -20.25 (E7) reflects expected continued losses on the earnings side. No multi-year EPS figures are provided to assess earnings trajectory more directly.

Operating margin is -66.9% (E11) and net profit margin is -226.7% (E12), with return on equity at -58.4% (E13) — all deeply negative. Gross margin is positive at 25.8% (E10) but comes nowhere near covering operating costs. The company is heavily lossmaking on every profitability measure provided.

Total cash of $349.39M (E16) far exceeds total debt of $24.11M (E17), a strong net-cash position, and a current ratio of 6.08 (E19) signals ample short-term liquidity. The reported debt/equity of 3.05 (E18) is the one cautionary figure and sits oddly against the low absolute debt level. Ongoing operating losses will steadily erode this cash cushion over time.

Forward P/E is negative at -20.25 (E7), so earnings-based valuation is not meaningful, while price/book of 2.44 (E8) applies to a company posting -58.4% ROE (E13). Market cap of $1.94B (E6) against only ~$0.1-0.2B of revenue (E24) implies a steep price/sales multiple. The analyst mean target of $5.33 (E3) is ~32% above the $4.05 price (E2) but rests on just 3 analysts (E23) with no consensus rating (E22).

Free cash flow is -$59.49M and operating cash flow -$53.29M on a TTM basis (E14, E15), so the business is consuming cash from operations. The $349.39M cash balance (E16) provides multi-year runway, but the cash-generation quality itself is poor and negative. Both cash-flow metrics agree directionally, supporting high confidence.

The evidence describes BigBear.ai's AI decision-intelligence products for national security, supply chain, and digital identity (E25) but provides no data on market share, competitive dynamics, customer concentration, switching costs, or differentiation. There is no basis to judge the existence or durability of a moat. This dimension is rated insufficient_data rather than guessed.

The 52-week price change is 0.0% (E21), yet at $4.05 (E2) the stock trades near its 52-week low of $3.01 (E5) and well below its 52-week high of $9.39 (E4), and a beta of 3.08 (E20) signals extreme volatility. Coverage is thin at 3 analysts (E23) with no consensus rating (E22), though the mean target of $5.33 (E3) implies modest upside. These signals are genuinely mixed, so the rating is neutral.

Multiple concrete red flags are present: negative free and operating cash flow (-$59.49M and -$53.29M; E14, E15), declining revenue (-0.9% YoY and the drop to ~$0.1B in 2025; E9, E24), deeply negative operating, net, and equity returns (-66.9%, -226.7%, -58.4%; E11, E12, E13), and a negative forward P/E (-20.25; E7). A very high beta of 3.08 (E20) and a reported debt/equity of 3.05 (E18) add volatility and leverage flags. The vague news headlines (E26-E30) are not treated as risk evidence.
